viva.question: Why does a stack validate brackets in linear time?
expected_points: each character is pushed or matched at most once
extra memory grows with nesting depth rather than with repeated scans
a final empty stack means every opener found a closer
the whole string is processed in one forward pass

viva.question: What breaks on a lone closer or an opener left unclosed?
expected_points: a closer with an empty stack has no matching opener
openers left on the stack at the end never found closers
balance alone is not enough if types or order are wrong

viva.question: Why must the popped opener match the closer's type?
expected_points: nested brackets require last-in openers to close first
a type mismatch means the nesting order is wrong
the stack top is exactly the most recent unmatched opener
crossing pairs would pop a different type than the closer expects
